A 37-year-old primigravida at 30 weeks' gestation presents to the emergency department with
worsening upper abdominal pain over the past hour. She reports initial dull stomach pain approximately
6 hours ago that has progressed and localized to the upper abdomen. She experienced one episode of
emesis en route to the hospital. Her medical and family histories are unremarkable. She is in a
monogamous relationship with her husband. She denies tobacco or alcohol use. Her only medications
are folic acid and prenatal vitamins. Her vital signs show a temperature of 38.5°C (101.3°F), heart rate
of 100/min, and blood pressure of 141/73 mm Hg. Physical examination reveals right upper quadrant
tenderness but is otherwise normal. Laboratory findings are as follows: | Hemoglobin | 13.1 g/dL | | --- |
--- | | Leukocyte count | 17,000/mm3 | | Serum | | | Urea nitrogen | 20 mg/dL | | Creatinine | 0.8 mg/dL | |
Alkaline phosphatase | 79 U/L | | Bilirubin | | | Total | 1 mg/dL | | Direct | 0.3 mg/dL | Urinalysis
demonstrates mild pyuria. What is the most likely diagnosis? Answer Choices: (A) Pancreatitis (B)
Ovarian torsion (C) Acute cholecystitis (D) Acute cholangitis (E) Diverticulitis (F) HELLP syndrome (G)
Appendicitis (H) Hepatic abscess (I) Pyelonephritis (J) Gastritis
 A. Ovarian torsion

B. Gastritis
C. Acute cholecystitis
D. Pancreatitis
E. Hepatic abscess
F. Diverticulitis
G. Appendicitis
